title: Variance and standard deviation of a random variable

draft.title: Variance and standard deviation of a random variable
card: Variance measures how spread out X is around its mean. Formula: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]².
E(X²) = Σ x² × P(x). Square each value first, then multiply by its probability and add. Then subtract the square of E(X).
The standard deviation is the square root of the variance: SD = √Var(X). It is in the same units as X.
Example: P(0) = 0.5 and P(2) = 0.5. E(X) = 1 and E(X²) = 0 × 0.5 + 4 × 0.5 = 2. So Var(X) = 2 − 1² = 1 and SD = 1.
draft.remember: Var = E(X²) minus the square of E(X). SD is its square root.

a.q: X has P(1) = 0.5 and P(3) = 0.5. So E(X) = 2 and E(X²) = 5. What is Var(X)?
a.why: Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]² = 5 − 2² = 1. The value 3 comes from subtracting E(X) instead of its square.

b.q: A spinner gives X = 0 with probability 0.6 and X = 5 with probability 0.4. What is the variance of X?
b.why: E(X) = 5 × 0.4 = 2. E(X²) = 25 × 0.4 = 10. Var(X) = 10 − 2² = 6. The value 2.45 is the standard deviation √6, not the variance.
b.clue: Find E(X) and E(X²) first, then subtract.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: Var = 5 − 4 = 1 in (a), and 10 − 4 = 6 in (b). The card's worked example is also correct.
